questions.q: What is the difference between a matching rule and a duplicate rule in Salesforce?
options: A matching rule merges records; a duplicate rule deletes them
A matching rule applies only to Leads; a duplicate rule applies only to Accounts
A matching rule defines when records count as likely duplicates; a duplicate rule decides what happens when a match is found
They are two names for the same setting
questions.explain: Matching rules define how records are compared; duplicate rules use them and decide the action (allow with alert, or block) plus optional reporting.

questions.q: Why can a matching rule find duplicates that GROUP BY Name cannot?
options: Matching rules can use fuzzy matching, so 'Acme Corp' and 'Acme Corporation' can be flagged as likely duplicates
GROUP BY cannot be used on the Account object
Matching rules run faster than SOQL
GROUP BY Name only returns records created today
questions.explain: GROUP BY groups only identical values, so it catches exact-name duplicates; fuzzy matching rules recognize near matches.

questions.q: Which objects store the duplicates found by a duplicate rule that has the Report option enabled?
options: The Recycle Bin
The Account and Contact objects themselves
Duplicate matches are never stored
DuplicateRecordSet and DuplicateRecordItem, which you can query with SOQL
questions.explain: Reported matches are written to DuplicateRecordSet and DuplicateRecordItem, giving you a queryable list of suspected duplicates.

questions.q: Why do duplicate rules not replace human review?
options: Rules can only run once per year
Rules only identify candidates; a person must judge whether records are truly the same entity and decide which data survives a merge
Human review is required by Salesforce before any record can be created
Rules automatically delete every match, so nothing is left to review
questions.explain: Two records with the same name may be different real companies, so a person makes the final call on which record survives.

questions.q: What happens to a duplicate rule with the Block action when a Data Loader insert matches an existing record?
options: The row is silently deleted from the CSV
The row is loaded anyway and merged automatically
The row fails with a duplicate error and appears in the error file, since API loads can trigger duplicate rules
Duplicate rules never apply to API loads
questions.explain: Duplicate rules can run on API loads, so blocked rows fail and are reported in the Data Loader error output unless the load is set up to allow duplicates.
